record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: For the Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_θu)(t) with smooth data and a uniform mesh I_h, let u_h \in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) be the collocation solution and let u_h^{it} be the associated iterated collocation solution. Does the optimal local error estimate proved in Theorem 2.2 still hold for this more general equation when b(t) is not identically zero?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.2 Assume that the given functions g, K0 and K1 in the VFIE (1.3) are arbitrarily smooth, with b(t) \equiv 0, and let uh \in S(−1) m−1(Ih) be the collocation solution to (1.3) corresponding to the m Gauss points {ci} in (2.2), with uniform mesh Ih.

Open Problem 2.1 Let uit h be the iterated collocation corresponding to the collocation solution uh \in S(−1) m−1(Ih) (defined in (2.12)), and assume that Ih is a uniform mesh. Does the optimal error estimate of Theorem 2.2 remain true for the more general VFIE (1.3) with (smooth) b(t) \equiv 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation with vanishing delay
$$u(t) = b(t)\,u(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_\theta u)(t), \qquad t\in I:=[0,T],$$
where
$$(Vu)(t) = \int_0^t K_0(t,s)\,u(s)\,ds, \qquad (V_\theta u)(t) = \int_0^{\theta(t)} K_1(t,s)\,u(s)\,ds,$$
the delay function $\theta:I\to I$ is smooth, strictly increasing, satisfies $\theta(0)=0$, $0<\theta(t)<t$ for $t\in(0,T]$, and $0<\theta'(0)<1$ (so $\theta$ vanishes at $0$); the data $b,g\in C^\infty(I)$ and $K_0,K_1\in C^\infty(D)$ on the appropriate triangular/relevant domain $D$.

Fix an integer $N\ge 1$ and let $I_h$ be the uniform mesh $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$, $t_n=nh$ with $h=T/N$, and set $\sigma_n:=(t_{n-1},t_n]$. Define the piecewise-polynomial space (discontinuous at mesh points)
$$S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) := \{v:I\to\mathbb{R} : v|_{\sigma_n}\in\mathcal{P}_{m-1},\ n=1,\dots,N\}.$$
Choose $m$ distinct collocation parameters $0<c_1<\cdots<c_m\le 1$ taken to be the $m$ Gauss points (the zeros of the shifted Legendre polynomial of degree $m$), and let
$$X_h := \{t_{n,i}=t_{n-1}+c_i h : n=1,\dots,N;\ i=1,\dots,m\}.$$
The collocation solution $u_h\in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h)$ is defined by enforcing
$$u_h(t) = b(t)\,u_h(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu_h)(t) + (V_\theta u_h)(t) \quad\text{for all } t\in X_h.$$
The associated iterated collocation solution is
$$u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t) := b(t)\,u_h(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu_h)(t) + (V_\theta u_h)(t), \qquad t\in I.$$

It is known that when $b(t)\equiv 0$, on a uniform mesh and with $m$ Gauss collocation points, the iterated collocation solution attains the optimal local superconvergence estimate
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\bigl|u(t_n)-u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t_n)\bigr| \le C\,h^{2m}.$$

Question: Does this optimal local error estimate continue to hold for the general equation above when $b(t)\not\equiv 0$ (with $b$ smooth)? That is, with the same uniform mesh and $m$ Gauss points, is there a constant $C>0$ independent of $h$ such that
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\bigl|u(t_n)-u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t_n)\bigr| \le C\,h^{2m}\,?$$
artifact.category_tag: Collocation methods for delay Volterra integral equations
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (e.g., Ming, Huang, Zhao 2018; later papers on quasi-geometric and quasi-graded meshes) has obtained optimal local superconvergence results for delay VFIEs with proportional delay $\theta(t)=qt$ on quasi-geometric meshes (with Radau II points) and discussed cases $b(t)\not\equiv 0$, but no source clearly settles the specific question of whether the order-$2m$ local error bound for the iterated collocation solution at Gauss points on a uniform mesh extends from $b\equiv 0$ to general smooth $b$. The status of this precise question therefore remains unclear from the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Optimal superconvergence results for Volterra functional integral equations with proportional vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a technique for optimal convergence orders of collocation methods on quasi-geometric meshes; for m Radau II points the collocation solution may attain superconvergence at nodes.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress on optimal superconvergence for VFIEs with vanishing (proportional) delays, but on quasi-geometric meshes with Radau II points rather than uniform mesh with Gauss points.

status_evidence.title: Superconvergence in Collocation Methods on Quasi-Graded Meshes for Functional Differential Equations with Vanishing Delays
status_evidence.snippet: Studies optimal orders of global and local superconvergence on quasi-graded meshes for functional differential equations with delays vanishing at t=0.
status_evidence.claim: Investigates superconvergence for vanishing-delay functional equations but in the differential setting and on quasi-graded meshes.

status_evidence.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems for collocation and iterated collocation solutions of VFIEs with vanishing delays, including the case b(t) not identically zero.
status_evidence.claim: The question of extending the optimal iterated-collocation local error estimate to b(t) not identically zero is posed as an open problem.
